source.title: Understanding Stability of Outer Nesterov Momentum on Stochastic Pseudo-Gradients
source.authors: Nishant Sharma; Laura Gomezjurado Gonzalez; G. Talluri; S. Chandar; Hiroki Naganuma

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices; no truncation or document mismatch is evident.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures training dynamics and loss at CIFAR checkpoints and language-model checkpoints, but studies stability of outer Nesterov updates rather than the listed random-initialization training-error claims.
record.gate_note: The paper’s reported amplification and spread-cost measurements bear on V5’s learning-rate/stability dynamics at checkpoints, but not V1–V4 or V6. The CIFAR training recipes and checkpoints are setup, not results about training error from random initialization. Cited findings about catapults and edge of stability are not this study’s results. Figure values are largely plots without a textual assignment of exact values to individual settings; no numeric rows are extracted from those plots.
record.test_reason: The study measures perturbation amplification and loss due to disagreement across stochastic two-phase optimizer runs. These do not test V5's recovery above an initial stability limit, curvature reduction, or full-batch sharpness tracking a stability threshold. Section 7 explicitly leaves catapults and edge-of-stability behavior with outer momentum open. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the inner trajectory acts as a random operator, and stability depends on its noise relative to the outer update's noise budget. Checkpoint experiments largely match the predicted hyperparameter trends, while spread cost need not track amplification. The authors explicitly leave outer-momentum catapults and edge-of-stability behavior unestablished and acknowledge that their local analysis does not capture longer-term recovery from instability.
record.recipe_differences: The study tests stochastic two-phase SGD with outer Nesterov momentum and checkpoint perturbation amplification/spread-cost measurements, rather than gradient-based training from random initialization and training classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome depends on outer momentum, number of local steps, inner batch size, worker count, total-batch splitting, outer learning rate, and checkpoint/model. The text reports some runs diverged, with the number surviving varying by setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Checkpoint perturbation amplification generally increases with outer momentum, responds to local-step count differently at small and large inner batches, and decreases with worker averaging. Splitting a fixed total batch does not improve it. Spread cost often follows these trends, with checkpoint- and model-dependent exceptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For stochastic two-phase SGD with outer Nesterov momentum, finite-horizon perturbation amplification and disagreement-related loss depend jointly on momentum, outer rate, local-step count, inner batch size and worker averaging.

record.problems: Network measurements are checkpoint-local and finite-horizon; the authors state the linearization is approximate along actual runs and that spread cost need not follow amplification at every checkpoint. Several settings diverged; some plotted measurements exclude diverged streams. Most exact network condition values are available only in figures, not as text or tables.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for every plotted hyperparameter value were extracted because exact values are figure-only and the text describes trends in aggregate; the source presents extensive checkpoint panels in Figures 4–5 and 9–23. Cited prior-work findings were excluded. Theory examples and exact random-quadratic model results do not measure versions V1–V6.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error from random initialization, including corrupted labels and dependence on model size or training recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Training degradation with depth and comparisons involving identity shortcuts, special initialization or normalization.
Activation-matched initialization, signal propagation, learning speed and trainable depth.

Recovery after exceeding the initial linearized stability limit, accompanying curvature reduction, larger-rate divergence, full-batch sharpness tracking the threshold, and divergence from below that threshold.
Batch normalization versus no normalization in training speed and learning-rate tolerance, including Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Remove all extracted V5 verdicts. States are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions, not findings that the study's own measured effects are absent. No missing result warrants a version-specific row.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error from random initialization; CIFAR-10/100 fit, label corruption, model size, stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU local minima and student width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, normalization, and training error.
Initialization schemes, depth, and training speed.

The reported network measurements use checkpointed stochastic two-phase SGD and amplification/spread-cost measures, not wide-network squared-loss learning-rate sweeps above a linearized stability limit, sharpness trajectories, or divergence probabilities. No learning-rate-induced catapult phase is tested.
Batch normalization and training speed/accuracy comparisons.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification of shared-minibatch perturbations over 20 outer steps along actual runs, varying outer momentum at fixed outer rate.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap confidence intervals over 48 minibatch streams; median width 0.027 in log10 Aθ(20)
rows.note: Text says that as β grows at a fixed outer rate, a setting turns from contracting to amplifying at most once. The plot supplies condition-level values without exact text-reported numbers.
rows.check: Perturbation amplification cannot establish V5. Figure 4(i) sweeps momentum at outer rates 0.25, 0.5 and 1; the row incorrectly restricts the panel to rate 0.5.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification of shared-minibatch perturbations over 20 outer steps, varying local-step count and inner batch.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap confidence intervals over 48 minibatch streams; median width 0.027 in log10 Aθ(20)
rows.note: Text states amplification contracts more as K grows at batches 8 and 16, and amplifies more at batches 1 and 2. Exact values by setting are plot-only.
rows.check: Perturbation amplification across batch sizes and block lengths does not measure any listed version. At b=1, K=28 and 56, reported amplification excludes diverged streams: 41 and 37 of 48 survive.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification of shared-minibatch perturbations over 20 outer steps, varying worker count.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap confidence intervals over 48 minibatch streams; median width 0.027 in log10 Aθ(20)
rows.note: The text states that more workers never raise amplification and that the setting shown amplifies with one worker but contracts with two or more.
rows.check: Worker-dependent perturbation contraction does not establish V5. Figure 4(iii) uses outer rate 0.25 and inner batch 2, rather than the recorded 0.5 and 4.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification of shared-minibatch perturbations over 20 outer steps while splitting a fixed total batch across workers.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrap confidence intervals over 48 minibatch streams; median width 0.027 in log10 Aθ(20)
rows.note: Text says splitting a fixed total batch did not lower amplification in any setting of Figure 4; at long blocks the more split configurations amplify more.
rows.check: Fixed-total-batch perturbation amplification does not measure any listed version. For the 8×1 split, amplification excludes diverged streams at K=28 and 56; the frozen calculation also redraws diverged inner trajectories.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured spread cost across 32 independent runs from different seeds after 20 outer steps, varying outer momentum.
rows.measure: Spread cost, loss due to disagreement between runs
rows.note: Text states spread cost rises with β; plot-only values are not reported numerically in text.
rows.check: Spread cost measures disagreement-related loss, not recovery or sharpness dynamics in V5. Figure 5(i) includes outer rates 0.25, 0.5 and 1, rather than only 0.5. Settings whose averaged model leaves the basin are marked rather than assigned plotted spread costs.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured spread cost across 32 independent runs after 20 outer steps, varying local steps and inner batch.
rows.measure: Spread cost, loss due to disagreement between runs
rows.baseline: K=1 for the relative spread-cost panel
rows.note: The text says spread cost first rises at every inner batch as K grows, then keeps rising for b ≤ 4 and turns down at b = 8 and 16.
rows.check: Spread cost relative to K=1 does not measure any listed version; its batch-dependent trend is not partial evidence for V5.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured spread cost across 32 independent runs after 20 outer steps, varying worker count.
rows.measure: Spread cost, loss due to disagreement between runs
rows.note: Text states spread cost falls with W.
rows.check: Reduced spread cost with more workers does not establish recovery above a stability limit or another listed effect.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured spread cost across 32 independent runs after 20 outer steps while splitting a fixed total batch across workers.
rows.measure: Spread cost, loss due to disagreement between runs
rows.note: Text states spread cost is not lowered by splitting a fixed total batch.
rows.check: Spread cost under total-batch splitting does not measure any listed version. At 8×1 and K=56, the value uses 28 surviving runs after 4 of 32 diverged.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification during a continuation at three outer settings, with one or two workers.
rows.note: Text describes loss and spread-cost consequences; exact amplification curves are plot-only.
rows.check: Continuation amplification does not establish V5 without an identified initial stability threshold and the specified recovery or sharpness dynamics. Amplification is Figure 24(c); panels (a) and (b) measure loss change and spread cost.

rows.subject: ResNet-20
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification during a continuation at three outer settings, with one or two workers.
rows.note: Text describes loss and spread-cost consequences; exact amplification curves are plot-only.
rows.check: Continuation amplification does not measure a listed version. Amplification is Figure 24(f); panels (d) and (e) measure loss change and spread cost. This ResNet-20 uses group normalization in place of batch normalization.

rows.subject: Pythia-70m
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification during a continuation at three outer settings, with one or two workers.
rows.note: Text says loss falls at every setting over these 100 outer steps, and spread cost stays far below training progress.
rows.check: Falling loss during a checkpoint continuation does not establish V5's threshold or recovery dynamics. Amplification is Figure 24(i); panels (g) and (h) measure loss change and spread cost. Pythia loss is evaluated on 128 held-out sequences, and only 18.9 million parameters are updated.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification over 20 outer steps across outer learning-rate and momentum settings.
rows.note: Text states contracting region grows with worker count; at every W its boundary falls from large α at small β to small α at large β.
rows.check: A finite-horizon perturbation contraction boundary is not V5's sharpness trajectory or initial linearized stability threshold.

rows.subject: CIFAR MLP
rows.operation_detail: Measured amplification over 20 outer steps across inner batches and local-step counts.
rows.note: Text says the contracting region shrinks to nothing at b=1 as K grows; barely moves at b=4; and keeps its size at b=16.
rows.check: Batch- and block-dependent perturbation boundaries do not measure any listed version. Entirely diverged settings are marked separately in Figure 23.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
